youtube-caption-extractor.languageBehavior: Defaults to en; prefers manual exact match, then ASR exact match, then falls back to the first track.
youtube-caption-extractor.requestStrategy: Tries IOS, ANDROID_VR, then MWEB player clients until caption tracks are found; downloads json3 timedtext.
youtube-caption-extractor.browserFit: Published entry is CommonJS and upstream recommends server-side use because browser calls face CORS; a bundler/bridge would still be required for the current MV3 extension.

youtube-transcript.languageBehavior: Exact language is strict; with no language it takes the first advertised track.
youtube-transcript.requestStrategy: ANDROID InnerTube first, then watch-page fallback; downloads XML timedtext.
youtube-transcript.browserFit: Small ESM/CJS package with a custom fetch hook, but direct MV3 use still needs browser host/CORS validation.

youtube-transcript-plus.languageBehavior: Exact language is strict; with no language it takes the first advertised track; listLanguages exposes track kind.
youtube-transcript-plus.requestStrategy: Watch page for API key, ANDROID player request, then XML timedtext; optional retry/cache hooks are disabled in this benchmark.
youtube-transcript-plus.browserFit: Node >=20 package; no browser export or ready-to-load MV3 bundle is declared.

youtubei.js.languageBehavior: Transcript language selection uses human-readable menu labels rather than BCP-47 codes.
youtubei.js.requestStrategy: Creates an Innertube session, requests video info/next data, then calls get_transcript.
youtubei.js.browserFit: Ships a browser bundle, but upstream documentation requires requests to go through a server proxy. This is not equivalent to dropping the bundle into the current MV3 extension.
